I do some non-zero amount of hiring for my company. Corporate HR does most of it, but for entry level jobs that will almost certainly be local hires they refer a set of candidates to regional offices who then conduct in person interviews and pick who they like. I've had a mixed bag of referrals in the past, but holy hell, yesterday's negress took the cake.

The job was for a junior office administrator. Secretary basically, only not assigned to any one person but the office as a whole. The past couple I've hired have been recent college graduates, just looking to get their feet wet and put something on the page. So I was optimistic when I saw the file for yesterday's interview. Her resume said she had a college degree from one of the local universities, which is usually good. The college kids that apply for such a job with us are usually grounded: They know that they're not going to walk out of an average school with a run of the mill degree into some high power position, but that our company has a good reputation and they can lose their professional virginity with us, work hard and either promote to something they'd really like to do or springboard to someone else with a nice referral from a respected name.

When the candidate arrived all that optimism was immediately lost. We're the kind of place where suits are still common, and oxford shirt and tie for men and skirt/slacks and blouse for ladies is the minimum standard. In walks a "robust" black lady not remotely meeting the standard. The first thing out of her mouth was, "Uh-oh, I feel like I'm under dressed. They had just told me to wear a collared shirt, I didn't know ya'll was Mad Men up in here. Oooh, someone should be embarrassed for steering me wrong."

She was technically wearing a collared shirt: Flip-flops, way too tight jeans, and an oversized purple and yellow polo shirt that said, "juicy."

I've cut some people some slack for being undressed before and given them a chance, especially if they're young and inexperienced since I usually have no idea what HR told them ahead of time. So if a kid shows up in sharp slacks and a golf shirt, for example, I try to give them a chance. Holy hell, though? Who in their right mind would think this was proper dress for any job interview, let a lone one in a high end professional office setting? I knew immediately this wasn't going to go well. Ideally, I'd be able to have just said so right there, but unfortunately in this day and age I had to still waste my time with a full pointless interview to avoid discrimination allegations.

We started with talking about why she wants the job, like I always do. This woman's answer was a five minute ramble about how the state was going to, "Take away (her) checks," if she didn't try to find work and made multiple references to "(her) man" being, "a lazy piece of shit."
